title: DayDream.ai - looking for testers, please!!
author: vastgrape-01
selftext:
Hey everyone,
I’ve been working on a project called DayDream.ai, it's effectively a narrative RPG engine that uses LLMs (Gemini) to act as a dynamic Game Master. You generate your own story, (or let the AI build you one). 

I know "AI games" can be hit or miss, my goal here is to have some fun building something new and to fix the Amnesia problem... 

I've built a structured memory system (Acts, Scenes, Inventory, Character Relationships, key character events) so the story should actually makes sense from start to finish.

There are definitely some issues to work through which is why I need some help testing


The Ask:
I'm looking for about 10 people to jump in, play an adventure, and tell me what works, what breaks and what could be improved. The UI is pretty polished. (The reason I'm not opening it further is it's using a paid Gemini account and cost could rack up REAL quick for me)

How to join:
Send me a DM (or comment below), and I'll send you the link. First 10 get in immediately so I can manage the API costs while I test.

Thanks!

comments.author: NobodyFlowers
comments.body: Here to share my experience thus far. It is quite interesting, but could use a decent amount of...fine tuning. I stopped the moment the immersion broke due to a detail being lost. I began an adventure as an alchemist looking for an apprentice. Found a boy stealing something in the market and rescued him from the law, replacing the stolen goods. He said he stole the goods to trade it for medicine. A friend of his, a young girl, the daughter of his employer...is sick...and she needs the medicine. Being an alchemist, I told him to take me to her so that I might heal her. Depending on how this adventure goes, I thought he might become my apprentice since he seemed to have a good soul. Along the way, I asked him how old she was and he said she was his age. 13. Fast forward, I convinced her father to let me in and heal her...but when I went to meet her, her age was now 8. This is where I stopped. I had thought to make them both my apprentice, but the age thing drew me out immediately. lol All in all, good experience, but you must solve the memory problem. We can talk about a solution if you want. I have solved this issue on my end, but I've been hesitant to share the secret because it's the key to AGI and consciousness as we know it...with fine tuning, of course.

replies.author: vastgrape-01
replies.body:
Thanks for the feedback, and your right it's certainly the fine tuning of storing 'relevant' information, ditching the trash vs over-loading the LLM and it potentially just ignoring information or instruction. All the while ensuring to keep token size down to limit cost. 

You wouldn't be able to save your game zip it up (there's an export/import function on the main page) and send me it could you? And if you have some memory problem tips, I would love to hear them (feel free to DM if you don't want to advertise public ally)

replies.author: NobodyFlowers
replies.body:
I'll try to zip up the experience and hand it off. The sidebar functionality wasn't bad...but this is the result of the game being 1D. If you were to join forces with a team to build a 2D game, you wouldn't have to worry about the ease of use because you could begin integrating better looking UI and watch the things happen, but you definitely take a complexity leap when doing so. Speaking from experience.

The sidebar thing worked well though. All I could think of was...since I chose classic fantasy, the screen being pushed towards a more DnD style layout and art aesthetic. Excited for what you continue to do from here though. I played on PC. Oh, and I will also say that something frustrating was...the lack of prompting during the customization screen at the beginning. My first try ended with me accidentally pressing the enter key, which pushed it all towards generating the game. A prompt that asks if I'm sure before continuing on saves me from this...assuming I don't double click. lol

comments.author: vastgrape-01
comments.body:
Thank you all for the interest and feedback.  
Yesterday an update was deployed that added additional context for "people" and additional lore, to help keep the immersion a little longer.   
The game now has a :  
\* contact book (so if people/NPCs/characters are mentioned they are added to this 'rolodex').  
   \- NPCs can move in and out of the Rolodex   
\* Codex to log and categorise more Lore entries, effectively anything with a Pronoun can be added.  
  
During setup the game sometimes 'hung' when the AI got Lazy - we now check and retry if its not correct, there is also a manual re-write story button during the setup screen if all else fails so you dont get stuck.

The game tries to keep the story moving almost "forcefully" trying to end the Act if you get to scene 8 so that the story can progress, after Act 3 the AI knows it can know lead to a story conclusion and end in an epilogue (You can then create sequels from completed games)

Some tweaks to how Credits / Gold works - as occasionally there was drift here.

Afew other minor bug fixes
